title: Memory layer stack

basis: Architectural metaphor, not an exact chip package or measured memory hierarchy.

Constraints: no lettering, words, numbers, symbols, labels, captions, equations, logos, watermarks, badges, interface panels or corner marks. Subject: a compact exploded assembly of four simple square wafer-like memory layers, seen from a stable three-quarter isometric angle, vertically separated by modest even gaps. The lowest layer is a graphite outlined thin base with eight short broad connector tabs visible along the front and side edges, shown as physical details rather than an exact chip package. The three upper layers are plain pale planes with graphite edges. One short vermilion ribbon-like connector bridges the nearest corner of the top two layers; this is the only red element. No traces, circuit routes, tiny component forest, arrow or labels. The stack must feel physically coherent, airy and architectural, not a scientific cutaway.
